fields.description:
Four independent definitions of "this blocker no longer blocks", with three different memberships:

- `graph/_ready.py:26` `{"closed"}`
- `graph/_unblock.py:26` `{"closed", "deleted"}`
- `graph/_graph.py:107` `("closed", "deleted")`
- `_engine_support/next_batch.py:30` `{"closed", "done", "completed", "deleted"}`

`done` and `completed` are NOT in the status vocabulary (`types.py:21`,
`schemas/common.schema.json:9`) — unreachable branches.

Reproduced empirically in a throwaway store: with a ticket blocked by a `deleted` ticket,
`next-batch` offered it while `ready` withheld it. The ordinary path is safe because `delete`
unlinks peers; only "link to an already-deleted ticket" triggers the split.

Scope clarified during approval. `ready` and `next-batch` answer DIFFERENT questions by design —
`ready` has zero file-impact logic; `next-batch` adds conflict-aware batching keyed solely off
declared `file_impact`. That difference is correct and documented. This ticket does NOT merge the
two commands; it unifies the one predicate they both depend on.

Maintainer decision: the terminal set is `{closed, archived, deleted}` — each represents a terminal
state. This CHANGES behaviour in three places: `ready` gains `archived` and `deleted`;
`_unblock`/`_graph` gain `archived`; `next_batch` gains `archived` and loses the phantom values.

Note `_ready.py`'s docstring already says a blocker must be "closed (or tombstoned / missing)",
which reads as though `deleted` should count — the code and its own docstring already disagree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] One shared terminal-state predicate, imported by all four sites
- [x] The phantom `done`/`completed` values are removed
- [x] A test asserts `ready` and `next-batch` agree on a ticket blocked by a deleted ticket
- [x] A test asserts the terminal set is a subset of the schema's status enum, so vocabulary drift fails fast
- [x] The `_ready.py` docstring matches the implemented rule
